obligation: Report to GSA IT (federal buildings)
citation: GSA BTTRG v3.0 section 1.6.1; Federal Facilities statements of work
trigger: Potential cyber incident involving GSA building systems, GSA data (including CUI drawings), or credentials of company staff with GSA access
deadline: Immediately
notify: GSA IT (per contract contact list) and the GSA contracting officer's representative
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if GSA systems, data, or staff credentials may be involved
owner: President, Federal Facilities (through the Federal Site Manager)

obligation: CUI handling non-compliance report
trigger: CUI drawings accessed, exfiltrated, or mishandled
deadline: By the method and timing the GSA agreement sets (the company reports immediately with the GSA IT report)
notify: GSA contracting officer (disseminating agency)

obligation: Public safety customer notice (CJIS-based contract term)
citation: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6(a), applied by the 27 public safety customers' contracts
trigger: Suspected incident affecting a public safety building's doors, access logs, or physically secure location
deadline: Immediately and within 1 hour of discovery
notify: Agency security contact and facilities director (the agency handles its own CJIS reporting)
owner: Site Manager with the State and Local Government segment notice owner

obligation: State agency contract incident notice
citation: State cybersecurity exhibits (5 contracts); Florida worked example: exhibit required by Fla. Stat. 282.318(4)(h)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed security incident affecting agency systems, buildings, or data
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
notify: Agency information security manager and contract manager
owner: State and Local Government segment notice owner

obligation: County and city contract incident notice
citation: County and city security addenda (38 contracts)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed security incident affecting customer systems, buildings, or data
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
notify: Customer IT security contact and facilities director
owner: State and Local Government segment notice owner

obligation: University and school district contract incident notice
citation: Education contracts (21); universities designate the company a school official (34 CFR 99.31(a)(1)(i)(B))
trigger: Suspected or confirmed incident affecting campus systems, buildings, or student cardholder records
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
notify: University information security office and facilities; district technology director

obligation: FSP subscription customer notice (SL-2)
trigger: Security incident affecting FSP customer data
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirmation
notify: Customer administrators named in the subscription

obligation: State agency's own report (customer duty; Florida worked example)
trigger: Agency determines a ransomware incident or a severity level 3-5 cybersecurity incident
deadline: Agency reports no later than 48 hours after discovery (12 hours for ransomware); the company's notice must arrive well before that
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center and FDLE Cybercrime Office (by the agency); the company supplies facts
applies_at_this_tier: Customer duty - company supports with facts and timeline
owner: State and Local Government segment notice owner

obligation: Local government's own report (customer duty; Florida worked example)
trigger: County or municipality determines a ransomware incident or a severity level 3-5 cybersecurity incident
deadline: No later than 48 hours after discovery (12 hours for ransomware)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff (by the local government); the company supplies facts
owner: State and Local Government segment notice owner

obligation: Local government after-action report (customer duty; Florida worked example)
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident
deadline: Within 1 week after remediation (by the local government)
notify: Florida Digital Service (by the local government); the company supplies input

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the customer (Florida worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system the company maintains that holds customer personal information (cardholder records; face templates, which counsel treats as biometric data under 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI) and 501.702)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the 24-hour contract terms come first)
notify: The customer that gives notice to individuals; provide all information it needs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a third-party agent for customer data; counsel confirms whether each customer is a governmental entity under 501.171
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: State breach notification (each state)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents (definitions vary, including biometric data in some states)
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; for customer data the customer usually notifies and the company supports
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of the company's own personal information of Florida residents (employees, for example SSNs or background check data)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days with written good cause to the Department)
notify: Affected Florida residents (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity for its own data
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida (company's own data)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.6)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)

obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment found
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Investigation identifies covered equipment used as a substantial or essential component of any system
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: GSA contracting officer

obligation: Kaspersky covered article found
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: GSA contracting officer

obligation: FASCSA order article found
citation: FAR 52.204-30(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article or source subject to a FASCSA order used in contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: GSA contracting officer

obligation: Ransom payment restrictions (customers; Florida worked example)
trigger: Ransom demand affecting a state agency's or local government's building systems
deadline: State agencies, counties, and municipalities may not pay; the company must not pay on their behalf (POL-03 4.7)
notify: Customer leadership; law enforcement

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment for the company's own systems is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Law enforcement and CISA report (voluntary)
trigger: Intrusion into building control or access control systems
deadline: As early as practical, coordinated with affected customers
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until it takes effect. If finalized as proposed, the company would likely be covered (above its SBA size standard in a critical infrastructure sector; counsel to confirm)

obligation: Federal agency incident reporting (federal facilities)
citation: 44 U.S.C. 3554; OMB and CISA federal incident notification guidelines
trigger: Incident on a federal information system
deadline: Per the CISA Federal Incident Notification Guidelines (applies to agencies; not re-verified here)
notify: CISA (by the agency)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a federal agency; GSA reports incidents on its own systems after the company's immediate report (first row)
verified: false (guidelines not re-verified; not relied on)

obligation: FTI unauthorized disclosure
trigger: Unauthorized disclosure of FTI
deadline: Immediately, no later than 24 hours after discovery
notify: TIGTA and IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no FTI access (P03 C-GOVERNMENT-R02)

obligation: Inbound notice from subcontractors and vendors
trigger: Incident at a subcontractor or vendor affecting company or customer systems or data
deadline: Subcontractors within 24 hours; PACS, BAS, edge, and cloud vendors within 72 hours
notify: To the SOC; then the customer clocks in this matrix start for the company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual (POAM-012 extends the addendum to legacy subcontracts)

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
